7.2.3 Pleasant Hill, the project status from funding updates.

So the report before you today is related to the completion of the Pleasant Hill Village revitalization project.
This is the largest neighborhood renewal project that has been undertaken by the city of Saskatoon.
The project stem from the 2002 Pleasant Hill Low Clary plan which highlighted the need for reinvestment in the neighborhood.
Renewal of housing stock and to change perceptions of the neighborhood.
This project has appeared before city council numerous times over the years.
Namely in 2007 for the initial concept plan approval in 2009 for the enhanced concept plan approval, which enlarged the study area and added an extra development parcel.
In 2014 to amend the zoning of the development parcels increasing their density for desired uses.
Additionally, several of the development projects were presented to city council over the years and received approval for financial incentives under the innovative housing incentives policy.

Most recently, this was for the round peries elder lodge, comfy community homes and the turning their life around STC project, which was the last two were done through the Rapid Housing Initiative project.
The project milestones and the results can be reviewed in detail in the appendix two which is the closed out report.
But some highlights include this project now includes six new housing developments creating a total of 169 new units of housing.
It includes safe and affordable housing options being expanded within the neighborhood, especially those for seniors, elders and large families.

A new St. Mary school was developed which includes a wellness center day care and child health services and a more modern reenvisioned park space for community and neighborhood use that includes a community garden, walking paths and a welcoming neighborhood entrance sign.

The project took place with the partnership from many external and internal groups and especially noted like to mention the Pleasant Hill community review committee and the Pleasant Hill community association who worked in partnership with administration to guide the development.
We're very thankful for their continued leadership and participation over the several years that this project took to complete.

Total funding towards the project was approximately $8.3 million and this was used to assemble and subdivide land, demolish old buildings, address environmental remediation, upgrade infrastructure and create new park space.

The project generated an estimated $64.5 million of investment in this area and that included the investments from the city as well as other levels of government developers and nonprofit organizations which led to the development of the quality affordable housing options that are now in place showing confidence in the neighborhood and making significant improvements to the neighborhood infrastructure.
At this point, the Pleasant Hill village capital budget account has approximately $137,000 remaining unspent and the report recommends a way to use these funds.
Administration is recommending that the funds remaining in the Pleasant Hill capital budget account of $137,000 be returned to the neighborhood land development fund or be redirected by city council.
We are also recommending that a budgeted annual transfer of $34,000 from the public housing subsidy account cease in 2024 with the funds returning to the public housing subsidy account.
That is the presentation. I'm available for any questions.
